learning_extracted: A substrate_hash change is not evidence that the executed code changed. The arm_fingerprint globs (arm_fingerprint.py:65-70) are deliberately over-inclusive, an asymmetry documented at :14-17 as 'over-inclusion -> false misses only'. That is correct for its DESIGNED purpose (arm-reuse cache validity, where a false miss is free) and WRONG when the field is repurposed as a divergence detector, where over-inclusion converts directly into false positives. The defect is in the reuse, not the field.

The D3 triage test needs a fourth question, asked BEFORE the sweep's sec-4 'where does the split fall' test: does the split reflect a change on the EXECUTED path at all? Recoverable cheaply by recomputing the fingerprint over the driver's import closure. On 782 that single question answers the whole autopsy.

The five benign channels the sweep ruled out (globs, scoped, machine_class, driver_script_in_substrate_hash, __pycache__) are all WITHIN-RUN variation. The channel that explains 782 is a BETWEEN-RUN property of the instrument -- the glob's scope relative to the closure -- which no within-run constancy check can see.

Parallel development in globbed directories is the generating mechanism: all three moved files belong to other sessions' work (SD-070, EXQ-783, SD-068). On a heavy-development day this fires against every long run on the fleet regardless of what that run touches -- predicting that the sweep's '2026-07-18 alone produced 6 divergent runs' clustering is largely an artefact of development volume, not experimental fragility.
The prior 2026-07-18 cluster autopsy's substrate-equivalence reasoning was correct and is now independently verified at blob-OID granularity.

secondary_routing_recommendation.route: re-scan the 41 genuine sweep hits with a closure-restricted recomputation BEFORE the instrument fix
secondary_routing_recommendation.why_first: V3-EXQ-604c and V3-EXQ-778a are queued for autopsy (sweep sec 7 items 2 and 3) on the same premise that just failed on 782. Establishing the true base rate is pure analysis over existing artefacts -- no compute, no fleet -- and re-prioritises those two before autopsy effort is spent on them.
method_sketch: For each of the 41 genuine hits, resolve the driver from experiment_type, build its transitive static import closure PER TREE, intersect with arm_fingerprint._SUBSTRATE_GLOBS, recompute the byte protocol per band, and report whether the closure-restricted hash is constant.
Partition into true D3 (closure-restricted hash varies -- real loss of control) vs glob-scope false positive (constant). Re-rank the SEVERE routings on the true set only.
Handle the dirty-tree case explicitly: a hit whose hashes do not all reconstruct from committed trees (782's did) is unverifiable, not clean.
secondary_routing_recommendation.instrument_fix_note: The durable fix should be CLOSURE-RESTRICTED, not the whole-glob check proposed in sweep sec 8(a). Emitting substrate_divergent: true keyed on the current whole-tree hash would have fired on 782 and on every run co-resident with unrelated parallel development -- institutionalising this false positive as a standing warning. Sweep sec 8(b) (per-cell stamping; 'provenance granularity must follow the unit of COMPARISON') is CORRECT and unaffected: it is the SCOPE of the hashed set, not its granularity, that failed here. The two recommendations are orthogonal and both survive.
secondary_routing_recommendation.scope_limit: This autopsy adjudicates V3-EXQ-782 only. The other 41 hits are NOT adjudicated here; 782's glob-scope artefact is a reason to check them, not a demonstration that they are clean. A modification to an on-path file would be a genuine D3.
